articles.title: Seahawks will face a major dilemma if they sign Terrion Arnold
articles.standfirst: Seattle is reportedly working toward a deal with the former Lions cornerback, but he could be sidelined by the NFL before taking a single snap
articles.summary: Seattle is reportedly working toward a deal with the former Lions cornerback, but he could be sidelined by the NFL before taking a single snap
articles.body:
Terrion Arnold’s expected move to the Seattle Seahawks has become one of the NFL’s most unusual roster stories of the preseason.

Although reports say Seattle intends to sign the former Detroit Lions first-round cornerback, the deal still hadn’t been finalized as of Wednesday. NFL Network reports that once Arnold signs, he’ll immediately be placed on the commissioner’s exempt list, keeping him from practicing or playing.

That delay makes the situation even stranger because the Seahawks would be accepting financial responsibility for a player unavailable to practice or play.

Players on the exempt list continue to receive their contracts, with their salaries counting against the team’s salary cap. Seattle would therefore be using valuable cap space on a player it knows won’t immediately contribute on the field.

Still, there’s a potential reason for the Seahawks to accept that unusual arrangement. Arnold remains a young former first-round talent with two seasons of starting experience.

If Seattle believes he can eventually return to the field, signing him now could allow the organization to retain his rights and potentially add a talented cornerback later in the season.

Why Seattle is still considering Arnold

Seattle’s interest also has to be viewed alongside what happened in Detroit. The Lions released Arnold on June 29, the same day a Florida judge released him on a $1 million bond following his arrest.

Arnold faces eight felony charges connected to an alleged kidnapping and assault case in Florida. If convicted, he could face a life sentence. Arnold has maintained his innocence.

The Lions’ decision to release their 2024 first-round pick came despite the organization previously expressing support for him. Arnold had been a starting cornerback during his first two NFL seasons and was viewed as an important part of Detroit’s secondary.

Interestingly, Seattle general manager John Schneider appears to understand why Detroit decided to move on. In the latest episode of HBO’s Hard Knocks, Schneider discussed Arnold’s situation with special teams coordinator Jay Harbaugh.

When Harbaugh questioned why Detroit released the cornerback, Schneider acknowledged that Seattle probably would’ve made the same decision if Arnold had been on its roster.

That admission gives the potential signing an unusual dimension, as while Seattle isn’t necessarily disputing Detroit’s decision, they appear willing to evaluate whether Arnold can eventually provide value while his legal situation plays out.

Timing could ultimately determine whether the signing happens at all. NFL Network reported that Seattle is “working through the timing” of the deal and indicated that it could take some time. With Arnold expected to land on the exempt list, there’s little incentive for the Seahawks to rush the transaction.

Arnold’s contract situation adds another wrinkle. He’s entering the third year of his rookie deal, which runs through 2027. There’s also a fifth-year option available for 2028 because he was a first-round selection.

This is clearly a gamble on future value rather than immediate production for Seattle. The Seahawks would be paying a player who can’t currently help them on Sundays, while also taking on uncertainty surrounding his legal case and potential league discipline.

If Arnold eventually becomes available, however, Seattle could have a former first-round cornerback waiting in the wings.

articles.title: Bud Clark refuses to break after devastating injury ends his rookie season in heartbreaking Hard Knocks scene
articles.standfirst: The Seahawks rookie was in obvious pain, but somehow found a way to joke, reassure everyone around him and share a touching moment with his young son
articles.summary: The Seahawks rookie was in obvious pain, but somehow found a way to joke, reassure everyone around him and share a touching moment with his young son
articles.body:
B ud Clark had every reason to fall apart. His rookie NFL season had essentially disappeared on one play, his right ankle was badly injured and he was being carted away from the field. Somehow, the Seattle Seahawks safety was still trying to make everyone else feel better.

New footage from Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the Seattle Seahawks captured the painful moments after Clark suffered a fractured ankle against the Tennessee Titans.

As trainers surrounded him and the reality of the injury began to sink in, Clark refused to let the fear take over. "We gravy, we gravy," he repeated, trying to reassure those around him even as he admitted how badly it hurt.

Bud Clark's son gave him something to smile about

T hen came the moment that made everything feel much more human. Back inside the locker room , Clark called his fiancée and young son.

Instead of allowing the conversation to become completely consumed by what had just happened, the injured rookie joked with his little boy after he asked who had hurt his dad. Clark playfully asked if he was going to go after the person responsible, and his son confidently said yes.

And then, in the wonderfully innocent way only a child can, his son moved on to something far more important in his world : he wanted to know whether Dad was still going to fix his bike.

For a few seconds, football, injuries and an NFL career disappeared. Clark wasn't a Seahawks safety whose season had just been taken away. He was simply a father talking to his little boy.

Seattle has since placed Clark on injured reserve, officially ending the second-round pick's rookie season before the regular season even began.

It was a crushing ending to the first chapter of an NFL dream, but Hard Knocks captured something statistics never could. Clark's ankle may have broken, but in one of the hardest moments of his young career, he refused to let the rest of him break with it.

articles.title: New Seahawks owner's unexpected ‘betrayal’ leaves fans in shock
articles.standfirst: Vinod Khosla still watches Pittsburgh every week, creating an awkward first controversy in Seattle
articles.summary: Vinod Khosla still watches Pittsburgh every week, creating an awkward first controversy in Seattle
articles.body:
Vinod Khosla has only just taken control of the Seattle Seahawks , but his first days as owner have already produced an unexpected controversy that has little to do with football operations.

Khosla , who completed a $9.6 billion purchase of the franchise with his family, surprised supporters during his introductory press conference by revealing that he remains a longtime Pittsburgh Steelers fan.

“I also happened to come to this country in ’76 when the Steelers were winning Super Bowls,” Khosla said. “So actually I was originally and still am a big Steelers fan.”

He then added: “Also, little known fact, but I still watch all the Steelers games, too.”

The admission quickly raised eyebrows in Seattle, particularly because the Steelers are responsible for one of the most painful defeats in Seahawks history.

Pittsburgh beat Seattle in Super Bowl XL, a loss that remains a sore point for some fans because of the officiating controversies that surrounded the game.

Khosla ’s connection to Pittsburgh, however, goes back decades. He moved from India to the United States in 1976 to attend Carnegie Mellon University, arriving at a time when the Steelers were dominating the NFL.

Pittsburgh won four Super Bowls in six seasons during that era, with Terry Bradshaw leading one of the most successful teams in league history.

Seahawks fans question Khosla’s Steelers loyalty

That background did little to stop the reaction. “Ehhh. I get it but I feel like that’s something you keep a secret,” one fan wrote on X. Another said: “He probably should have kept that to himself.”

Khosla ’s NFL history isn't limited to the Steelers either. Before buying the Seahawks , he held a minority stake in the San Francisco 49ers , one of Seattle’s biggest NFC West rivals. That stake must be sold as he takes control of the Seahawks .

Still, there is no indication Khosla ’s previous allegiances will affect his commitment to Seattle. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell publicly backed the new ownership group after the sale was approved.

“They know our league well,” Goodell said. “They understand the passion of the NFL, they understand the 12s, they understand this Seattle community and the NFL.”

Khosla pushes back after comments cause stir

Khosla later responded to the criticism himself, arguing that his remarks had been blown out of proportion.

“What’s wrong with admitting my 1976-78 period in Pittsburgh (CMU) got me excited about the NFL?” Khosla wrote on X.

He also made clear where his priorities now lie, saying that continuing to watch Pittsburgh doesn't mean he won't “unconditionally ALWAYS as owner, want the Seahawks to win and have every edge up, EVERY TIME over every other team!!!!”

That may ultimately matter more than any old rooting interest. Seattle enters Khosla ’s ownership era as the reigning Super Bowl champion, creating immediate expectations for the new regime.

“The task ahead is actually pretty simple,” Khosla said. “Keep the winning streak alive. Get another Super Bowl.”

If Seattle continues winning, his Steelers fandom will probably become little more than an amusing footnote. If things go badly, though, Seahawks fans may not forget the admission quite so easily.

articles.title: Seahawks won’t miss Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III thanks to this stellar rookie with a massive future
articles.standfirst: The path to immediate playing time has become even clearer for the newcomer
articles.summary: The path to immediate playing time has become even clearer for the newcomer
articles.body:
T he Seattle Seahawks are entering the 2026 season with one of the NFL's strongest rosters and the confidence that comes from being the defending Super Bowl champions. Yet one of the biggest storylines surrounding the franchise is also one of its biggest questions: who will replace Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III?

According to a panel of NFL.com analysts , the answer may be a lot more exciting than many expected. When predicting the winners of the league's major individual awards for the upcoming season, the majority of NFL.com's experts selected Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price as the favorite to capture Offensive Rookie of the Year honors.

The path to immediate playing time has become

It's a bold prediction, but the circumstances in Seattle make it easy to understand why Price is generating so much buzz before taking his first regular-season snap. The Seahawks selected Price with the 32nd overall pick in April's NFL Draft, making him the second running back chosen in the first round. Since then, his path to immediate playing time has become even clearer.

Walker, who rushed for 135 yards and earned Super Bowl MVP honors in Seattle's championship victory, departed in free agency to join the Kansas City Chiefs on a three-year deal worth up to $43.05 million. While the Seahawks valued Walker's contributions , the organization ultimately chose not to match Kansas City's offer as it balanced other financial priorities across a championship-caliber roster.

Meanwhile , Zach Charbonnet remains on the physically unable to perform list while recovering from the ACL injury he suffered during Seattle's playoff run. His availability for the start of the season remains uncertain, and there is no guarantee he will return before midseason.

The result is a remarkable opportunity for Price

The players responsible for 1,757 of Seattle's 2,069 rushing yards last season and 17 of the team's 19 rushing touchdowns may not be available when the season begins. That leaves Price positioned to become the centerpiece of a rushing attack that was already one of the NFL's most productive units.

Seattle ran the ball 507 times in 2025, the third-highest total in the league. Even with offensive coordinator Brian Fleury replacing Klint Kubiak, the Seahawks are expected to maintain the run-first philosophy that helped power them to a championship. Left guard Grey Zabel has already made it clear that Fleury intends to keep that identity intact. “I love his run-first mentality, and we are going to enjoy it," Zabel said of Seattle's new offensive coordinator.

For a rookie running back, there may not be a better situation in the league. NFL.com's analysts pointed to that reality when making their Offensive Rookie of the Year selections. Price is expected to receive starter-level touches immediately, potentially handling 15 or more opportunities per game while operating within one of football's most stable organizations. He also benefits from playing alongside a roster loaded with proven stars, making it difficult for defenses to focus solely on stopping the run.

The opportunity is especially notable considering Price's college career. At Notre Dame, he spent much of his time sharing the backfield with Jeremiyah Love, a Heisman Trophy finalist who was selected third overall in this year's draft. While Price never had the chance to be a full-time featured back, he consistently flashed elite explosiveness whenever he touched the football.

Over three seasons with the Fighting Irish, Price averaged 5.8, 6.2 and 6.0 yards per carry. Each year, he produced at least one touchdown run of 54 yards or longer, reinforcing his reputation as one of college football's most dangerous big-play threats. Those explosive traits are exactly what Seattle hopes can help replace Walker.
